speaker: interviewer
text: Thanks for joining. In the simulation, what was the conflict really about?

speaker: candidate
text: It was not about code. Dana and Timur both wanted the product to last, they just had no shared rule for changes.

speaker: interviewer
text: What would you change for the next project?

speaker: candidate
text: I would set up a weekly review where anyone can propose a change, and we decide together what goes into the release.

speaker: interviewer
text: What could go wrong with that review?

speaker: candidate
text: It could turn into long meetings. I would cap it at thirty minutes and write the decision in one place.

speaker: interviewer
text: The Thursday run failed. What did you do the next morning?

speaker: candidate
text: Honestly, I told everyone to work harder and stay late. I did not have a plan for what to fix first.

speaker: interviewer
text: Your application mentions a mentoring plan that was rejected. What happened after that?

speaker: candidate
text: I was disappointed and stopped working on it. Another student restarted it a month later.

speaker: interviewer
text: And Timur, how did you treat him in the simulation?

speaker: candidate
text: I kept Dana's version and did not ask Timur what he needed. Looking back, I should have talked to him.

speaker: candidate
text: Dana owns the release, and I own the review notes. For Timur, I am not sure yet.
